cohort: This study included 80 parturients (40 in the TENS group and 40 in the no analgesia group) from the Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology (OBG), Shimoga Institute of Medical Sciences, Shivamogga, Karnataka, India.
finding: TENS provided satisfactory analgesia, significantly reducing pain scores during both the first and second stages of labour, without adversely affecting labour duration or neonatal outcomes.
mod_finding: No significant difference was found in the mode of delivery between the TENS and no analgesia groups.
